explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/522: Erdős and Offord showed the number of real roots of a random ±1 polynomial is (2/π + o(1)) log n. The statement takes real ±1 coefficients and counts real roots with multiplicity. It asserts the existence of o, p → 0 with P(|#roots/log n - 2/π| ≥ o(n)) ≤ p(n), i.e. #real roots / log n → 2/π in probability, which is the standard probabilistic meaning. Faithful.
